technical_and_design_decisions: Use Spring Integration Java DSL for module implementation to leverage fluent API and reduce boilerplate.
Adopt Spring Boot auto-configuration for each source/sink module to enable seamless integration with Spring Cloud Stream.
Leverage existing Spring Integration extensions: spring-integration-websocket for U1, spring-integration-aws for U2 and U4.
For Cassandra sink (U3), use Spring Data Cassandra with reactive support for high-throughput writes.
For HAWQ sink (U5), integrate with PXF (Pivotal Extension Framework) using Avro/Parquet serialization; implement custom PXF connector if needed.
For SOLR sink (U6), use Spring Data Solr with SolrClient for indexing operations.

Implement error channel (U7) as a global Spring Integration error channel with a custom exception hierarchy (GlobalException, DefaultException, ModuleSpecificException) and a router to direct errors to a configurable channel (e.g., topic.errors.stream.module).
Data partition strategy (U8) is already implemented in GA; only testing effort is required to verify dynamic adaptation when modules are added/removed.
All modules will be built with Java 17 and Spring Framework 6.x, using Maven for dependency management.
Integration tests will use Testcontainers for external dependencies (Cassandra, SOLR, LocalStack for AWS, HAWQ/PXF).
assumptions: Development team has strong expertise in Spring Integration, Spring Cloud Stream, and the target technologies (WebSocket, AWS, Cassandra, HAWQ, SOLR).
Required dependencies (Spring Integration WebSocket, AWS, Spring Data Cassandra, Spring Data Solr, PXF libraries) are available and compatible with Spring 6 / Java 17.
Existing CI/CD pipeline supports building, unit testing, and integration testing with Testcontainers.
AWS source/sink modules will use LocalStack for local integration testing; no actual AWS account required for development.
HAWQ/PXF environment is available for integration testing (either via a test instance or embedded).
Error channel implementation will be generic and not tied to specific modules; it will handle exceptions from any source, processor, or sink.
U8 (data partition strategy) requires only testing effort; no new code development.
Documentation includes JavaDoc, README updates, and sample configuration for each module.
Code review and merge effort is estimated as a cross-cutting activity.
Effort estimates are for a single developer; no pair programming or overhead for meetings included.
